title: How Late Further Cost Is Brought and What Is Accepted of It
content:
Further cost brought late in the plan's supplement window is accepted at a share of itself under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan, and a share standing unpaid on the enrolment lowers it further.

- Where the further cost is brought in the second half of the plan's supplement window, counted from the day of the most recent appraisal standing on the enrolment, and a share stands unpaid on the enrolment, it is accepted at the marketplace's late-arrears share of 85 percent.
- Where it is brought in the second half of that window and nothing stands unpaid, it is accepted at the marketplace's late-notice share of 90 percent.
- Where it is brought in the first half of that window, it is accepted in full.

### The window each plan publishes

| Plan | Supplement window, calendar days |
|---|---|
| Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan | 14 |
| Keyturn Shield 85 Host Plan | 21 |
| Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan | 30 |
| Keyturn Shield 75 Host Plan | 45 |
| Keyturn Shield 70 Host Plan | 60 |
| Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plan | 90 |

The cost is brought in the second half of the window when more than half that number of calendar days has passed since the day of the most recent appraisal standing on the enrolment: more than 15 days on the Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan, more than 7 on the Keyturn Shield 90 Host Plan, more than 45 on the Keyturn Shield 60 Host Plan.

### Boundary readings (hypothetical, on the Keyturn Shield 80 Host Plan)

| Days since the most recent appraisal standing | Unpaid on the enrolment | Accepted at |
|---|---|---|
| 15 | either | the whole of it |
| 16 | none | 90 percent |
| 16 | some | 85 percent |

At exactly half the window the cost still falls in the first half and is accepted in full.

### Where the facts come from

What stands unpaid is the amount owed by the host on the enrolment; where several appraisals stand on the enrolment, the days run from the most recent of them.
